# A platform primitive belongs to the codegen that emits it. Naming one from a
# build targeting a different platform has no answer, and inventing one emitted
# `<Switch onCheckedChange="...">` from a build that reported success.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out intrinsic.sngl
stderr 'platform primitive'
stderr 'android'
stderr 'targets html'

# A host's own widget is the same case from the other side: a `#[kt.native]`
# composable -- which is what android declares Switch as, and what a program
# writes for one the platform never heard of -- is called only by the platform
# whose screen is Kotlin.
! sngl generate --lang none --platform html --out out native.sngl
stderr 'kotlin''s Switch'
stderr 'targets html, which renders no kotlin widget'

# Its own platform still builds both.
sngl generate --lang kotlin --platform android --out out2 intrinsic.sngl
exists out2/MainScreen.kt
sngl generate --lang kotlin --platform android --out out3 native.sngl
exists out3/MainScreen.kt

-- intrinsic.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/android"

component main node {
    vbox {
        android.SnglDateField(label="when")
    }
}

window {
    main
}
-- native.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:platform/android"

component main node {
    vbox {
        android.Switch(checked=true, onCheckedChange=func(v bool) {})
    }
}

window {
    main
}
